drain_procedure.barrier: New dispatch on old rails is refused until every census row has a terminal ledger kind=complete|fail|drain. The barrier is a count: in_flight == drained and abandoned_without_record == 0, not a wall-clock guess.
drain_procedure.notes: The three-row census is a disclosed drain fixture covering the three named rails. It is not a claim that live Task/MCP/Databricks processes were inspected on this host.
steps: Freeze new ad-hoc dispatch: Task/MCP/Databricks adapters refuse a spawn that has no prior kind=claim.
Census in-flight work per rail (Task ids, MCP thread ids, Databricks active runs).
For each census row, append kind=drain outcome=IN_FLIGHT_LEASED (still running) or ABANDONED (process gone, no artifact). Never delete the census row as a substitute.
Lease those unit_ids onto the typed work-unit queue; the shared completion reducer stays FALSE until a terminal complete|fail row exists.
Only after the barrier (every census row has a drain or terminal row) disable the old rails. Rollback re-enables them; the ledger is not unwritten.

procedure: Treat the source JSONL as immutable; refuse dest==source.
For each physical line, json.loads. Parseable objects become ledger kind=fold records carrying source.raw and source.sha256.
Blank lines and malformed JSON are classified drops persisted to a distinct drops JSONL, never silently omitted.
Ledger records are hash-chained (prev_hash, event_hash). The source file is not opened for write.
Conservation: input_events == output_records + classified_drops. Reverse concatenation of source.raw in line_no order reconstitutes the slice.

ledger_record_shape.hash_chain: event_hash = sha256(canonical JSON of the record minus event_hash); prev_hash of seq=1 is 64 zero nibbles

legacy_root.question: Design the path from today's ad-hoc dispatch (Task subagents, [REDACTED] MCP threads, Databricks jobs) to ONE work-unit contract: what adapter each existing rail needs, how in-flight work is drained rather than abandoned, and how the existing event log is folded into the new ledger WITHOUT rewriting history.

rails.adapter: Wrap every Task spawn: before the host starts the child, write a ledger claim {unit_id, substrate, rail=task_subagent, external_ref=task_id, lease_owner}. The child argv/prompt is required to echo that unit_id; a spawn without a prior claim is refused by the adapter, not launched.
rails.claim: kind=claim, unit_id from WORK-UNIT-CATALOG, external_ref=task_id, dedupe_key=(unit_id, attempt). Two dispatchers racing the same unit_id: exactly one claim row wins (first append with that dedupe_key); the loser records kind=claim_rejected.
rails.complete: On Task return, append kind=complete|fail with the same unit_id and the child's exit/sentinel. Missing sentinel is fail, not success. Re-running an idempotent unit appends another complete row; it must not rewrite the first.
rails.drain: Census running Task ids from the host. Each id with no terminal ledger row is leased (kind=drain, outcome=IN_FLIGHT_LEASED) or, if the process is gone with no artifact, kind=drain outcome=ABANDONED. Killing a Task without one of those two rows is forbidden.
rails.existing_rail: Task-tool / nested-agent dispatches that today carry no catalog unit_id and no ledger claim

rails.adapter: Map thread_id -> unit_id at open: ledger claim with rail=codex_mcp, external_ref=thread_id, substrate=cloud-batch or local-serialized as the MCP session dictates. Cancellation or network fault must either reclaim the thread by id or append ABANDONED; a running thread with no owner is a drain miss.
rails.claim: kind=claim with external_ref=thread_id and unit_id. Re-open of the same thread_id after a crash is resume (kind=resume), not a second unit.
rails.complete: MCP terminal payload folds to kind=complete|fail. A cancelled stream without reclaim or ABANDONED is incomplete; the shared completion reducer returns FALSE.
rails.drain: List live MCP thread ids. For each: if ledger already terminal, skip; if thread still running, lease; if thread missing, ABANDONED. Never drop a thread_id from the census without a drain row.
rails.existing_rail: [REDACTED] MCP threads (thread_id) that today can die mid-request and leave a running thread with no owner

rails.adapter: jobs.submit is preceded by a ledger claim {unit_id, rail=databricks_job, external_ref=run_id, idempotency_key}. The Databricks idempotency key IS the unit_id+attempt, so a retry cannot mint a second run for the same claim. Timeout is read back from the run, never assumed.
rails.claim: kind=claim with external_ref=run_id (filled in after submit returns) and job_id. A submit that fails before run_id exists still appends kind=claim_rejected so the queue is not silent.
rails.complete: Terminal Databricks life-cycle (SUCCESS/FAILED/TIMEDOUT/CANCELLED) maps 1:1 onto kind=complete|fail. Polling is the adapter's job; the ledger does not infer completion from wall clock.
rails.drain: jobs.list-runs --active-only is the census. Each active run_id without a terminal ledger row is leased; a run that vanished without terminal state is ABANDONED with the last known life_cycle_state. Runs are not cancelled as a drain shortcut.
rails.existing_rail: Databricks Jobs (job_id + run_id) used as a portable batch rail without a work-unit claim or timeout readback

work_unit_contract.claim_record: ledger kind=claim with fields unit_id, rail, external_ref, dedupe_key, lease_owner, prev_hash, event_hash
work_unit_contract.delivery_guarantee: at-least-once plus idempotent units: a duplicate dispatch may append a second claim_rejected or a second complete row, but must not rewrite a prior ledger line or a prior artifact. Exactly-once is NOT claimed; the claim record + dedupe_key is the mechanism that makes a second dispatcher lose.
work_unit_contract.idempotence: A unit is idempotent when re-running it with the same unit_id leaves the artifact byte-identical (or appends an explicitly versioned successor path). Units that cannot meet that bar are classified non-idempotent and MUST be claimed with a unique attempt suffix so a retry cannot clobber the first artifact.
